memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"As the LORD commanded Moses, Aaron put the manna with the tablets of the
covenant law, so that it might be preserved. The Israelites ate manna forty
years, until they came to a land that was settled; they ate manna until they
reached the border of Canaan. (An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.)"
- Ex 16:34-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Forty years. Every single morning.

Stop and consider the scale of that. Roughly fourteen thousand mornings, for a
nation of hundreds of thousands, in a desert. Not one morning missed. Children
were born, grew up, married, and had children of their own, and every one of
those days the bread was there.

The chapter began with people convinced God had brought them out to starve. It
ends with the quiet record of four decades of unbroken provision.

Notice when it stopped: when they reached a land that was settled. Joshua 5:12
records that the manna ceased the day after they ate the produce of Canaan. God
did not withdraw it early, and He did not continue it once it was no longer
needed. He provides exactly as long as the need lasts.

Jesus drew on this chapter directly. After feeding the five thousand, the crowd
asked about the manna their ancestors ate. He answered, "I am the bread of life.
Whoever comes to me will never go hungry" (John 6:35). And He noted the sober
truth: their ancestors ate manna and still died. He offers bread of a different
order.

Forty years of faithfulness in the desert, pointing to a greater bread that
lasts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God provided so consistently that you have stopped noticing?
2. Have you come to Christ for the bread that manna only pointed toward?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for provision I have taken for granted. Lord Jesus, You are the
bread of life; feed me with Yourself. Amen.
